raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`ChainAllocator.alloc_extend_swa_tail` is the decode-side preallocation path for hybrid full/SWA models under unified memory: the owner band takes virtual pages for the whole sequence, and the window band binds only the pages of the live window tail. The pages to bind were picked on the device, with `torch.unique` over the tail of the extend kernel's output followed by `torch.isin` against the new virtual pages. Both are data-dependent and synchronize the host with the device, so admission in the scheduler stalled behind the in-flight forward.

## Modifications

This change is expressed on the allocator structure introduced in #46976, where `alloc_extend_swa_tail` hands `_allocate` a `tail_pages` closure that selects the window pages to bind.

Pick the tail's new pages on the host instead. The extend kernel hands the j-th new virtual page to sequence page `first_new_page + j`, and `num_swa_pages`, the number of tail pages that are new, is already computed on the host for admission pricing. The tail's new pages are therefore the last `num_swa_pages` entries of the new virtual pages, so `tail_pages` returns that slice (and an empty slice when no new page lies in the tail) with no device round trip. The pages bound, the prefix pages left alone, and the admission price are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerics change: the window binds the same pages as before. Ran the unit tests that drive `alloc_extend_swa_tail` against this branch on one GPU; the swa-tail test also passes unchanged on main, as expected for a sync-free rewrite that binds the same pages:

```
pytest test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_swa_tail_allocation.py
1 passed, 16 subtests passed
pytest test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_decode_prealloc_no_host_sync.py \
       test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_tri_pool.py \
       test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_allocator.py
63 passed, 105 subtests passed
```

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results).
- [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR.

detail.title: [Perf] unified-memory: Bind the SWA tail's new pages without a host sync in alloc_extend_swa_tail

files.patch:
@@ -795,13 +795,16 @@ def alloc_extend_swa_tail(
                 prefix_lens=prefix_lens_cpu,
             )
 
+            # Only NEW pages need binding; a tail page carried in from the prefix
+            # is already bound on the swa side. The extend kernel gives the j-th
+            # new page to sequence page first_new_page + j, so the tail's new
+            # pages are the last num_swa_pages of them. Slicing them on the host
+            # keeps admission free of host syncs: a device-side match
+            # (torch.unique) blocks the scheduler behind the in-flight forward.
             def tail_pages(out: torch.Tensor, new_pages: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
-                if swa_tail_len == 0 or new_pages.numel() == 0:
-                    return new_pages[:0]
-                tail = torch.unique(out[-swa_tail_len:] // self.page_size)
-                # Only NEW pages need binding; a tail page carried in from the
-                # prefix is already bound on the window.
-                return new_pages[torch.isin(new_pages, tail)]
+                if num_swa_pages > 0:
+                    return new_pages[-num_swa_pages:]
+                return new_pages[:0]
 
             return self._allocate(
                 full_tokens=num_new_pages * self.page_size,
